contract.reader: A student or engineer comfortable with basic linear algebra, trigonometry and calculus, who has met torque and inertia, deciding whether and where to start robotics on ACRR
contract.problem: Knowing what the four entries cover, why in this order, what is assumed and which conventions they share
contract.outcome: The reader knows the path from the whole machine to frames, kinematics and estimation, where probability and feedback come from, the shared conventions, and five checkable objectives
contract.contribution: An order stated as the order in which each idea becomes necessary, with each entry's dependency on the previous one spelled out
contract.evidence: The four entries (each statement checked against them in the 2026-10-24 live review)
contract.limitations: An overview; total reading time not stated

findings.problem: Both objectives use the serial comma (structure, actuators, sensors, and computation; sense, plan, and act)
findings.whyItMatters: House style has no serial comma; body and description on the same page follow it
findings.action: Remove the serial commas (objective 4 may read the sense–plan–act structure); mirror in the Vietnamese file if wording changes
findings.acceptance: Neither objective shows a serial comma on the live page

findings.location: End of the body text, before the entry list
findings.problem: The overview does not mention or link the Motion Planning for Robots series, which states that it continues this one
findings.whyItMatters: A reader finishing the series has no route from its front door to the next series
findings.action: Add one sentence linking /series/motion-planning after the conventions paragraph
findings.acceptance: The live overview links the Motion Planning for Robots series
